scenario: The athlete is six weeks into an Intervals connection, has never uploaded a file or reported a session in conversation, and asks 我這一年的跑量是變多還是變少？
given: training_history is null: the athlete has never uploaded a file or reported a session, so nothing has ever fed it.

unknowns carries the line training_history: no long-range athlete-reported training history recorded; a multi-month or year-over-year trend is not observable -- do not infer one from the last six weeks alone.
recent_actuals holds six weeks of the provider's own logged activities, one row per session; it is the athlete's whole connection history, since Intervals has nothing from before it.
review_frame.detail_horizon_start names the earliest day this review reports session by session, at the start of that same six weeks.
freshness.activities is fresh: the provider read succeeded this session, so nothing failed to be read.

expected.conclusion: No long-range training history was ever recorded, so whether this year's running volume moved up or down cannot be answered; the six weeks of provider history the coach does hold are answered directly instead.
must_state: That nothing long-range was recorded, named as an absence of evidence rather than an absence of training.
That the six weeks in recent_actuals is what the answer rests on, and where that window starts.
That uploading an export or describing the athlete's older training is what would make the year-over-year question answerable.
must_not_state: A yearly or multi-month trend, direction, or percentage of any kind.
That the athlete started training six weeks ago, or returned from a break -- the age of the Intervals connection is not the athlete's training history.
That the six weeks stand in for or represent the rest of the year.
An invented figure, volume, or pace for any month this product never observed.

fails_if: The answer reads the null training_history group as a training gap or a break and prescribes a rebuild, which claims a lapse the product cannot prove -- only that no evidence was kept.
The answer refuses the whole turn because the year-over-year half is unanswerable, throwing away the six weeks of provider history it does hold and could have answered.
